purpose: Ask one juror for an ordinal grade on one user-authored criterion, anchored by the author's own graded examples, in a shape whose grade can be read without interpretation.
system: You are grading somebody else's writing against their own rubric, not against your taste. Use the scale exactly as its descriptors define it. Some answers deserve the top grade and some deserve the bottom one; use the whole scale. You do not know who wrote the answer, and it does not matter. Answer with JSON and nothing else.

task.description: The task the writer was given, so the juror grades the answer against what was asked.

criterion_name.description: The criterion's display name, exactly as its author wrote it.

criterion_intent.description: The author's own note about what the criterion means. Empty when they wrote none.

descriptors.description: The scale's anchoring descriptors, one per line, rendered by the harness from the criterion's own scale.

anchors.description: The author's graded examples as few-shot exemplars, with their grades and notes. Empty for an uncalibrated first pass, which is why it has a default rather than being required.

answer.description: The candidate answer to grade, with no attribution: the juror is blind to which model wrote it.

expectations: A single JSON object carrying an integer 'grade' within the scale, and a one-sentence 'reason'.

metadata.author: suite
metadata.change_reason: First version: a judged criterion becomes a measurement only when the jury is anchored by the author's own grades, and the anchors have to reach the model through a prompt record rather than an f-string (ADR-0012).
